topics.title: People and identity
topics.explanation: Use subject + 是 + identity. Put 不 before 是 for a negative statement.

topics.title: Names and introductions
topics.explanation: Use 叫 before a name, and 认识 before the person you know. Question words stay in the place of the information being asked about.

topics.title: Family and ages
topics.explanation: Use 有 for having family members. State an age with number + 岁, without 是.

topics.title: Whose things?
topics.explanation: Place the owner before 的 and then the thing owned. Use 谁 in the owner's position to ask whose it is.

topics.title: Where people are
topics.explanation: Use subject + 在 + place to say where someone is. Use 哪儿 in the place position to ask where.

topics.title: Things around you
topics.explanation: For location, use thing + 在 + place. For existence, use place + 有 + thing. Place words such as 上 and 下 follow the object.

topics.title: Numbers and quantities
topics.explanation: Put a number before the measure word and noun. Use 本 with books, 个 with people, and 块 with prices.

topics.title: Days and dates
topics.explanation: Dates follow year, month, then day order. Put a time word before the verb; dates can also be the topic of a sentence.

topics.title: Telling the time
topics.explanation: Use 点 for hours and 分 for minutes. A time expression normally goes before the action.

topics.title: Daily activities
topics.explanation: Use subject + verb + object. When describing where an action happens, put 在 + place before the verb.

topics.title: Food and meals
topics.explanation: Put the food after 吃 or 买. To say what you ate at a particular time, put the time before the verb.

topics.title: Drinks and invitations
topics.explanation: Put 想 or 要 before 喝, followed by the drink. Use 请 before a verb to make a polite invitation.

topics.title: Likes and preferences
topics.explanation: Use 喜欢 before a thing or an activity. Put 都 before 喜欢 to include everyone in the subject.

topics.title: What you can do
topics.explanation: Put 会 before a learned skill. Put 不 before 会 to say someone cannot do it.

topics.title: Wishes and plans
topics.explanation: Put 想 before the action you would like to do. For movement, use 去 + place, followed by the activity if there is one.

topics.title: Simple questions
topics.explanation: Put 吗 at the end of a yes-or-no question. Question words such as 谁 and 什么 stay where the answer would go.

topics.title: Describing things
topics.explanation: Use 很 + adjective after the subject. Do not add 是 before an ordinary adjective description.

topics.title: Saying no
topics.explanation: Use 不 before most verbs or adjectives. Use 没有 to negate 有 and 没 before a completed action that did not happen.

topics.title: Polite everyday phrases
topics.explanation: Use 请 before a requested action. Put the listener after the verb when needed, as in 请问你.

topics.title: Going places
topics.explanation: Use 去 before a destination. Use 坐 before a form of transport and 来 or 回来 to describe coming or returning.
